finding: Before this change, the casualty point and weapon helper published pickup results from admission checked before native action. Native inventory callbacks/mission event handlers can replace the point task; pre-action eligibility cannot authorize publishing the old result or point follow-through after that effect boundary. This is a synchronous native-effect boundary, not an assumption that ordinary unscheduled code is scheduler-preempted.
implementation: Point arrival retains an independent original public point-order copy. After TakeMagazine, original private brain, order, group/locality, epoch, operation generation, original deadline, route and lease must still match before reading/publishing the result.

If ammo context changed, retire only the original private brain and skip old visit follow-through. After the optional weapon helper, recheck before the point VISITED cleanup. A replacement installed brain remains protected by existing FINISH identity checks.

TakeWeapon retains its original public order and rechecks actor/group locality, brain/order, epoch, operation generation, original deadline, native route and movement lease before post-action observations/result publication. Refusal makes no inventory rollback or successor mutation.
The one-equipment-request-per-visit priority remains. No new worker, timer, retry, inventory action, route or deadline.
cost: Effect-bound metadata/route receipt reads only; no new periodic scan or geometry query. Reused existing native-route reader cost remains engine/route-size dependent and unmeasured.
limits: No delayed inventory acknowledgement is introduced. Immediate UNVERIFIED remains possible even when native effects arrive later.
Native callbacks and replacement races, delayed pickup/cleanup and physical return must be verified in-game; audits paused.
Identical external state rewrites cannot be distinguished by equality alone. This is not all-controller handover completion or whole LAMBS parity.
